comparability_rule: comparable_to_us is 'no' or 'yes' with a hand-written note for the products in REFERENCE_CAVEATS (an OTC, other-indication or other-formulation product, or a duplicate marketing authorisation of the originator), 'yes' when the first word of the EU product name equals the first word of a US NDA/BLA brand name of the molecule, and 'unknown' otherwise. It does not change the selection; compare_jurisdictions should show a caveat when it is not 'yes'.
eu_number_rule: Union Register open dataset (ods_products.json, Creative Commons Attribution 4.0): rows with Type Human carry EUNumber, the product page URI (html/h{n}.htm) and EMALink, the EMA EPAR page. An EMA product is mapped through its medicine_url equal to EMALink (case-insensitive, trailing slash and scheme ignored); when no EMALink matches, through an exact normalised product name, ignoring a trailing '(previously ...)' note, among Human rows (preferring Active rows; recorded as a name match). The h-page of every reference product is then fetched and its EMA number (dataSet_proc ema_number) and EU number (dataSet_product_information) are checked against the mapping.

rule_text: EMA medicines JSON rows with category Human and medicine_status Authorised. The INN field (international_non_proprietary_name_common_name) is split on ' / ', ',' and ' and ' (and on ';', which the JSON uses between the substances of a combination; this changes no match) and each part is normalised (lowercase, non-alphanumerics to spaces, spaces collapsed). A product matches a molecule when its INN set is exactly {molecule inn} or {molecule name} after the same normalisation (single substance only in v1; products whose INN set has more than one part and includes the molecule are combinations, excluded and counted). Among matches with generic = No and biosimilar = No, the reference product is the one with the earliest marketing_authorisation_date (ties: lowest EMA product number). Every other matching authorised product is recorded as an alternate; only reference products are built. Version 2 (salt-alias-v2): when the exact-INN rule finds no reference, a single-substance authorised product whose INN is the molecule's INN plus salt or hydrate words (kind salt) or the INN of its US adopted name (kind alias), with generic = No and biosimilar = No, becomes the reference (earliest marketing_authorisation_date, ties: lowest EMA product number); the other salt or alias products are alternates. Overrides: REFERENCE_OVERRIDES in tools/eu.py names the reference by hand for a few molecules (duloxetine: Cymbalta, the depression and pain product, not the earlier urinary-incontinence Yentreve; umeclidinium: Incruse Ellipta, the 2014 originator, not its 2017 duplicate Rolufta Ellipta); the products they displace become alternates.
